h: Farms, Foot Tunnels and River Boats
p: Canary Wharf is all glass towers and city workers in the week, but at weekends it takes on a much more relaxed, family-friendly vibe, and there's lots of surprising stuff close by.

Just south on the Isle of Dogs, Mudchute Park and Farm is a big city farm with sheep, goats, pigs and llamas, plus open parkland and views back to the towers. It's free to visit and a brilliant contrast to the shopping centre.

At the southern tip of the island, Island Gardens looks across the river to Greenwich, and the Greenwich Foot Tunnel takes you under the Thames to the Cutty Sark. Kids love the idea of walking under the river, and on the other side you've got the Royal Observatory, the National Maritime Museum and Greenwich Park all waiting.

If you'd rather travel above the water, Uber Boat by Thames Clippers runs river services from Canary Wharf Pier, making it a fun way to get to Greenwich or into central London. It's a cracking way to see the city from a different angle.

Every January, Canary Wharf hosts its Winter Lights festival, with light art installations dotted around the estate, which makes an after-dark visit really special. Throughout the year, there's also a public art collection scattered around the plazas and parks.
Being right in the business district, the area has loads of places to eat, from quick bites to sit-down restaurants. It's an easy add-on for a family day out.
Weekday sessions can feel quieter than you'd expect for central London, which is a bonus if your family likes a bit of space.
